title: WPMS/1179/2023 of VINOD CHANDRA BHATT Vs STATE BANK OF INDIA

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1179 of 2023
Vinod Chandra Bhatt ........Petitioner
State Bank of India and Another .....Respondents

Present:-
Mr. Pratul Kumar, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, Advocate for the respondents.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 By means of the instant petition, the petitioner
seeks the following reliefs:-
 "(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents no-1 do not deduct 50%
amount from the pension account of the
petitioner and do not credited in said
amount in the account of the respondent
no.-2.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents no-1 to decide the
representation dated 23/03/2023 of the
petitioner (contained as Annexure no.5 to
this writ petition) forthwith.

2
(iii) Issue any other relief, which this
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in
the circumstances of the case.
(iv) Cost of petition may be awarded in
favour of the Petitioner."
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. The petitioner was in Armed Forces, when his
wife filed an application under Section 125 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973, seeking maintenance. It
appears that the amount of maintenance was fixed and
when processes for realization of arrears of maintenance
was initiated by the wife of the petitioner, a compromise
was entered into between the parties, which is Annexure
No.1 to the petition. According to it, the petitioner had
agreed that he would continue paying 50 per cent of his
salary or gratuity, General Provident Fund, insurance,
etc., and also 50 per cent of his pension to his wife. Para
4 of this compromise also records that, in fact, the
deduction may be made at the level of Drawing and
Disbursing Officer, so as to be deposited in the account of
the wife of the petitioner. The petitioner retired from

3
Armed Forces in the year 2003. His pension and other
dues were deposited in the State Bank of India , Branch
Srinagar, Pauri Garhwal ("the bank"). It so happened that
in terms of the compromise, 50 per cent of the amount of
the pension, which the petitioner received, has been
deducted by the bank and it was deposited in the account
of his wife. The petitioner made a representation to the
bank that the amount may not be deducted from his
account as he is ready and willing to pay the amount
separately to his wife. When this application was not
decided, the instant petition has been filed.
4. On the last date, the Court had required the
respondent no1, Branch Manage, to appear personally
before the Court. She would submit that as per the
communication received from the Centralized Pension
Processing Centre, 50 per cent of the pension of the
petitioner is deducted and deposited in the account of his
wife.
5. At the very outset, the Court wanted to know
from learned counsel for the petitioner as to whether the
petitioner is not bound by the compromise, which he has
entered into with his wife, particularly, whether the
petitioner is not ready and willing to pay 50 per cent of

4
the amount of his pension to his wife, in terms of the
compromise? Learned counsel for the petitioner would
reply that the petitioner is ready and willing to pay 50 per
cent of his pension to his wife as maintenance. The Court
posed another question to the learned counsel for the
petitioner as to what is wrong if directly from the bank
level, the amount that is due to the wife of the petitioner,
is deducted from the account of the petitioner and
deposited in the account of his wife? There is no reply to
it.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the
respondent/bank would submit that, in fact, Para 4 of the
compromise empowers the Drawing and Disbursing
Officer to deduct the 50 per cent amount and pay it to the
wife of the petitioner. He would also submit that, in fact,
the Centralized Pension Processing Centre, Garhwal
Rifles, vide communication dated 18.06.2016, had
directed the respondent no.1/bank to pay 50 per cent of
the amount received by the petitioner directly to Smt.
Meena Devi, the wife of the petitioner. At the time of
hearing, learned counsel for the respondents has
tendered for the perusal of the Court, the letter dated

5
18.06.2016 of the Centralized Pension Processing Centre.
Paras 2, 3, 4 and 5 of it reads as follows:-
 "2. It is intimated that No 4067594L Veteran Nk
Vinod Chandra has again represented to this office that
his pension has been stopped by SBI Srinagar wef Mar
2016. The above named indl was transferred to pension
establishment wef 01 Mar 2003 and service pension
sanctioned vide PPO Para 1 (b) above.
 3. It is also intimated by chief Judicial Magistrate
Rudraprayag (Photocopy of court order No 19/2001 dt
13 Jul 2001 attached) that 50 % share of all financial
benefits due to her husband on retirement are to be
paid direct by your banker to Smt Meena Devi wife of
above named indl.
 4. In view of the above you are requested release is
pension at the earliest after doing necessary verification
as 0per court order.
 5. Account No of the Veteran 10972185912."
7. The petitioner had agreed to pay 50 per cent of
his salary, gratuity, other retiral dues and pension to his
wife. Today also a statement is given that the petitioner is
ready to keep his words and is ready and willing to pay 50
per cent of the pension as well. At the time of hearing, on
behalf of the respondents, a document has been placed,
by which the respondent no.1/bank has been directed by
the Centralized Pension Processing Centre, records of the
Garhwal Rifles to directly pay 50 per cent of the pension
of the petitioner to his wife. That is what is being done.

6
8. It is a writ petition. Why this jurisdiction has
been invoked, it is not even clear. Learned counsel for the
petitioner is not in a position to tell as to what is the
grievance of the petitioner. There is no reason to make
any interference in this petition. It appears that the
petitioner has some other motives to file the writ petition.
Accordingly, It deserves to be dismissed.
 9. The writ petition is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 15.05.2023
Ravi Bisht
